comparisons.peer_summary: Data Center net revenue increased 94% to $12.6 billion in 2024 from $6.5 billion in 2023, primarily driven by higher sales of AMD Instinct GPUs and AMD EPYC CPUs. Operating income rose to $3.5 billion in 2024 from $1.3 billion in 2023, mainly due to higher revenue partially offset by increased R&D investment.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVIDIA and AMD reported substantial double-digit growth in their Data Center segments for fiscal year 2024, driven by demand in specific high-performance computing areas. NVIDIA reported a 217% increase in Data Center revenue, fueled by enterprise software and consumer internet applications, with compute revenue up 244% and networking up 133%. Similarly, AMD reported a 94% increase in Data Center net revenue to $12.6 billion, primarily driven by higher sales of AMD Instinct GPUs and AMD EPYC CPUs. While both companies benefited from AI-related product demand (NVIDIA's AI infrastructure and AMD's Instinct GPUs), NVIDIA's growth magnitude was significantly higher (217% vs 94%), and NVIDIA explicitly highlighted networking revenue growth (133%) alongside compute, whereas AMD focused on the combined impact of GPUs and CPUs on revenue and operating income.

sentences.text: Data Center revenue for fiscal year 2024 was up 217%.
Strong demand was driven by enterprise software and consumer internet applications, and multiple industry verticals including automotive, financial services, and healthcare.
Data Center compute revenue was up 244% in the fiscal year.
Networking revenue was up 133% in the fiscal year.
Data Center net revenue of $12.6 billion in 2024 increased by 94%, compared to net revenue of $6.5 billion in 2023.
The increase was primarily driven by higher sales of AMD Instinct GPUs and AMD EPYC CPUs.

comparisons.peer_summary: Semiconductor solutions segment net revenue increased due to strong demand for AI networking products, partially offset by lower demand for broadband and server storage. Infrastructure software segment net revenue increased primarily due to contributions from VMware.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVIDIA and Broadcom (AVGO) identified strong demand for AI networking products as a key driver of their respective data-center-adjacent or semiconductor segment growth in fiscal 2024. NVIDIA's Data Center networking revenue increased by 133%, supporting its broader data center compute growth. Broadcom's Semiconductor Solutions segment net revenue also increased due to strong product demand for networking products, specifically AI networking products, although this was partially offset by lower demand for broadband and server storage. Both disclosures highlight AI networking as a specific, high-growth component of their semiconductor portfolios, though NVIDIA reports this as part of a unified Data Center segment with massive overall growth, while Broadcom reports it within a larger Semiconductor Solutions segment that includes offsetting declines in other areas.

sentences.text: Networking revenue was up 133% in the fiscal year.

Net revenue from our semiconductor solutions segment increased due to strong product demand for our networking products, primarily AI networking products, partially offset by lower demand for our broadband and server storage products.

comparisons.peer_topic: Data Center and AI (DCAI) Revenue and Volume Analysis
comparisons.peer_summary: DCAI revenue decreased $4.2 billion from 2022, driven by lower server demand; server volume decreased 37% due to a softening CPU data center market, while server ASPs increased 20% due to a lower mix of hyperscale customer revenue and a higher mix of high core count products.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVIDIA and Intel (INTC) discussed the performance of their data center/server businesses in fiscal 2024, but they faced divergent market conditions. NVIDIA's Data Center revenue grew 217%, driven by strong demand for AI infrastructure. In contrast, Intel's Data Center and AI (DCAI) revenue decreased, with server volume dropping 37% due to a softening CPU data center market. While NVIDIA thrived on AI and compute demand, Intel reported a decline in server volume, although it noted that server ASPs increased 20% due to a mix shift toward high core count products. This highlights a significant divergence in the data center semiconductor market in 2024, with AI-driven growth for NVIDIA versus volume decline for Intel's traditional CPU business.

sentences.text: Data Center revenue for fiscal year 2024 was up 217%.

Server ASPs increased 20% from 2022, primarily due to a lower mix of hyperscale customer-related revenue and a higher mix of high core count products.
